S1.why: Under a bracket a bare count plus adjective is how a Turkish label reads; the tiles are the noun, so naming them again would only crowd 12 characters.

S2.why: An invitation in the siz imperative the vocab uses (sağlayın); "saklamak" (to keep, as in iOS "Mesajları Sakla") is the one saving verb used in every key; exactly 20 characters.

S3.s: %lld ücretsiz Cutling’inizi kullandınız. Hepsi ücretsiz kalacak ve çalışmaya devam edecek.
S3.back: 5 free Cutling-your-(acc.) you-used. All-of-them free will-stay and to-working continue will.
S3.why: Turkish keeps the noun singular after a numeral, so it holds for any count; future tense (kalacak, edecek) makes the reassurance a promise rather than a rule.

S4.why: Plain siz statement; the suffix sits on Cutling, never on the number, so no vowel harmony depends on the value.

S5.why: Turkish names the whole before the part, so the total comes first and positional placeholders are needed; "tanesini" carries the case ending so no suffix ever lands on a digit.

S6.why: The -lik suffix ("5.000 kişilik salon") is the native way to size a space; short noun phrase like the other bold row lines.

S7.why: "Metin" and "görsel" from the vocab, singular after numerals; "en fazla" (at most) left out because at the moment of asking it reads as a cap, and the number already says it.

S8.why: Turkish lists with a comma and a single "ve" before the last item, no serial comma.

S9.s: Tek satın alım, Apple Hesabınızla üçünde de geçerli.
S9.back: Single purchase, Apple Account-your-with three-of-them-in too valid.
S9.why: "Apple Hesabınızla" exactly as the vocab writes it; "üçünde de" points back at the three devices in the bold line instead of naming them twice.

S10.why: The fixed Turkish phrase for a one-off charge, the opposite of "aylık" (monthly); 18 characters.

S11.s: Abonelik yok, reklam yok, üyelik yok.
S11.back: Subscription none, advertisement none, membership none.
S11.why: The repeated "yok" is how a Turkish speaker says it out loud; "üyelik" is the everyday word for signing up to a service.

S12.why: The wording Turkish iOS apps use for the App Store restore action, title case like Apple's Turkish buttons; 25 characters, one over the 24 budget, and no shorter form is recognised for this action (flag for review).

S13.why: The progressive passive is how iOS Turkish shows work under way (Yükleniyor…), with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Action, then the price marked with the S10 phrase so it reads as paid once; no suffix touches the price, so any currency format works; 25 characters plus the price (the smoother "Tek Seferlik %@ ile Kilidi Aç" ran to 27).

S15.why: The standard iOS Turkish label for unlock, same verb as S14.

S16.why: What iOS Turkish says when a person puts something off (Şimdi Değil); it leaves the door open instead of refusing.

S17.why: The iOS Turkish label for a close button.

S18.why: Warm and plain; "hepsi" takes in the five tiles and the whole new grid at once; 17 characters.

S19.s: Teşekkürler. Cutling’e ve onu tek başına yapan kişiye destek oldunuz.
S19.back: Thanks. Cutling-to and it alone making person-to support you-became.
S19.why: Thanks first, then what the money did, in the siz past tense; "tek başına yapan kişi" says one person makes it without a sob story.

S20.s: Tekrar hoş geldiniz. Önceki satın alımınız geri yüklendi.
S20.back: Again welcome-you. Earlier purchase-your back was-loaded.
S20.why: "Tekrar hoş geldiniz" is the set Turkish welcome back; "geri yüklendi" repeats the S12 verb so the person sees the link did what it said.

S21.why: Same whole-then-part order as S5 with positional placeholders; passive here because VoiceOver describes the tiles' state.

S22.s: %lld Cutling’iniz var. Artık %@ Cutling’lik yer var.
S22.back: 5 Cutling-your exists. Now 5,000 Cutling-worth room exists.
S22.why: Turkish uses the singular after every numeral, so 1, 2, 5 and 21 all read correctly; S6's "Cutling’lik yer" reused so the room has one name.

S23.s: Cutling’in kilidi açıldı. Artık %@ Cutling’lik yer var.
S23.back: Cutling-of lock-its was-opened. Now 5,000 Cutling-worth room exists.
S23.why: The app's name in the genitive marks this as the app being unlocked; second sentence repeats S22's room phrase.

S24.why: Impersonal passive, so no one is blamed; "satın alma" names the act of buying, while "satın alım" (S9, S12) is the purchase a person owns.

S25.s: App Store’a şu anda ulaşılamıyor. Biraz sonra tekrar deneyin.
S25.back: App Store-to this moment cannot-be-reached. A-little later again try-you.
S25.why: App Store keeps its English name with the Turkish suffix after an apostrophe (Store’a, from the spoken "stor"); "biraz sonra" is calmer than "daha sonra".

S26.s: App Store bu satın almayı onaylamadı.
S26.why: States what the store did, not what the person did; same "satın alma" as the alert title.

S27.s: Bu cihazda giriş yaptığınız Apple Hesabında Cutling satın alımı bulunamadı.
S27.back: This device-on sign-in you-made Apple Account-in Cutling purchase could-not-be-found.
S27.why: "Giriş yap" and "Apple Hesabı" from the vocab sentence; "bulunamadı" is how Turkish reports an empty search; 75 characters.

S28.s: Ücretsiz sürüm %lld Cutling saklar. Cutling’in kilidini bir kez açarak dilediğiniz kadar saklayın.
S28.back: Free version 5 Cutling keeps. Cutling-of lock-its one time by-opening wished-by-you as-much keep-you.
S28.why: Siri reads this aloud, so two whole sentences in the siz form, with the same "sakla" verb and "kilidini aç" as the sheet; 98 characters.

S29.why: "4/5" is how Turkish screens show a used-of-total count; order matches English so no positional forms needed.

K1.why: "Yer" is the room S6 and S22 already name, and a slot fills where a Cutling cannot; "Kilidi açın" tells the person what tapping does; 37 characters.

M1.why: Verb-led command name in title case, as macOS Turkish names its windows and menu items; 22 characters.

M2.why: M1 with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: The vocab's plural list title with an adjective in front, so the row reads as a label and M4 supplies the count.

M5.why: A state, not an event (açık, not açıldı); the possessive points at Cutling, whose section the row sits in.

M6.s: Tek satın alımla Cutling’in kilidi iPhone, iPad ve Mac’te açılır.
M6.back: Single purchase-with Cutling-of lock-its iPhone, iPad and Mac-on opens.
M6.why: "Tek satın alım" as in S9; the locative goes on the last item only (Mac’te, from the spoken "mek"), as Turkish does with a list.

M7.s: Bu Apple Hesabıyla iPhone, iPad ve Mac’te kilidi açık.
M7.back: This Apple Account-with iPhone, iPad and Mac-on lock-its open.
M7.why: Same list and state word as M5 and M6; "Hesabıyla" is the vocab's account word with its consonant softened before the suffix.

M8.s: Cutling’i ücretsiz olmadan önce satın aldınız, bu yüzden kilidi hep açık kalacak. Teşekkürler.
M8.back: Cutling-(acc.) free becoming-before you-bought, this because-of lock-its always open will-stay. Thanks.
M8.why: Fact, consequence, thanks, in the siz past; "hep açık kalacak" promises it stays as it is; 95 characters.
